conviction_note: Three revisions drive this: the bar is guided DOWN (company Q1 FY27 guide $0.33-0.39 vs $0.45 a year ago, consensus $0.35 / $940.9m, EPS estimates flat for 60 days), the only demand evidence dated after MillerKnoll last spoke on 2026-06-24 is positive (HNI's 30 July primary release: Workplace Furnishings orders +5% organic with the y/y rate ACCELERATING over the most recent five weeks, and H2 guided to high-single-digit organic; StoneX's August dealer survey reporting resilience), and MillerKnoll has an unrecognised IEEPA refund claim on 'substantially all IEEPA tariffs paid' while a direct import peer, RH, booked $55.1m of exactly those refunds in the overlapping quarter. I hold expected_move (+3.5) ABOVE the findings sum (+2.1) deliberately and say why: this name's own reaction distribution has a 10.83% median absolute move, coverage is three analysts, 7.29 days to cover sits on 624k shares a day, and the last two prints were +12.0% and -22.4% - there is no mechanism here for a 2-point reaction. The offsetting caveat is real and is why I am not at +6: the last two prints were decided by EPS versus guide, not by orders (Q3 FY26 had North America orders +13.1% and the stock fell 22.4% on a $0.02 EPS miss), so if the quarter lands a cent light the same asymmetry works against me, which is what the low end of my band carries.
bar: Company guide for Q1 FY27 of $928-968m net sales and $0.33-0.39 adjusted diluted EPS (https://news.millerknoll.com/2026-06-24-MillerKnoll,-Inc-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results, 2026-06-24), corroborated by sell-side consensus of $940.9m and $0.35 (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/millerknoll-earnings-in-focus-as-new-ceo-faces-margin-test-93CH-4909208, 2026-09-21). Two agreeing sources, so no small-size cap applies. I size print_vs_bar against the $940.9m revenue consensus, which sits below the guide midpoint of $948m.
positioning_check: 4.00m shares short, 5.99% of float, 5.86% of shares outstanding, short ratio 7.29 days to cover, up from 3.87m the prior month (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mlkn/statistics/, read 2026-09-21). Not a crowded short by level, but 7.29 days to cover on 624k shares of average daily volume (sealed baseline) means covering is slow and a positive print has a mechanical bid behind it - that is a reason to hold my long size rather than shrink it, and it would be a reason to shrink a negative. The baseline's 25-delta skew is +9.66 vol points, nominally 'downside paid', and I am explicitly going the other way: the option market here is 75 contracts of total open interest with an ATM bid-ask 80% of mid, so that skew is two stale quotes and not a statement of what anyone paid. For the same reason I do not anchor on the baseline's 16.78% 'event implied move'; my anchor is the name's own realised reaction distribution (median |move| 10.83% over seven prints).

findings.finding: MillerKnoll has submitted refund claims on 'substantially all IEEPA tariffs paid' and had recognised nothing as of the FY26 10-K (20 July 2026), while CBP's CAPE refund channel has been paying out on a 60-90 day cycle since 20 April 2026 and a direct import peer, RH, recognised $55.1m of IEEPA refunds in the quarter ended 1 August 2026 - four weeks BEFORE MillerKnoll's quarter closed on 29 August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MillerKnoll has no prior refund print. The nearest analogue is a below-operating-income item: the $92.3m of goodwill impairments taken in Q3 FY25 (2026-03-26 print, +10.69%), where the market looked straight through the non-operating charge. That says items below the line neither help nor hurt this name much on their own, which is why this is sized at a fraction of the dollars rather than at them. There is no stated path from a refund to the FY27 guide, so I file it as one_off and not as guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: The 10-K itself says 'the amount and timing of any refunds that may be realized remain uncertain', so no sell-side model can carry it - the Investing.com preview published this morning frames the quarter as a cost-inflation margin test and never mentions a refund, and the consensus EPS of $0.35 has not moved in 60 days. If the market had priced a refund, a name whose forward PE is 10.0 would not be down 10.9% over the month against -1.7% for its peer group, and the estimate line would have drifted up after RH's 10 September disclosure. Amount is unquantified by the company: MillerKnoll's disclosed NET tariff impacts were ~$7.0m (Q4 FY25), ~$8.0m (Q1 FY26) and ~$1.0m (Q2 FY26), which are after pricing offsets, so gross IEEPA duties eligible for recovery are larger than those figures but I will not invent the number - the band reflects that.
findings.independence: RH's 10 September 2026 shareholder letter is the independent second source and it is a different company and a different filing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001528849/000110465926106743/rh-20260910xex99d2.htm ($55.1m recognised in Q2, $13.9m more expected in H2). Third, CBP's own refund mechanics: https://www.ghy.com/trade-compliance/cbp-cape-ieepa-refund-progress/ (CAPE Phase 1 open 2026-04-20, refunds generally issued 60-90 days after acceptance, ~$128.68bn accepted for processing as of August 2026). No document is shared with any other finding in this file.

findings.finding: The only demand evidence dated after MillerKnoll last guided (2026-06-24) is positive and comes from the largest direct competitor's primary release: HNI's 30 July 2026 Q2 exhibit states Workplace Furnishings orders +5% organic, that 'over the most recent five-week period, the year-over-year segment order growth rate accelerated', and guides segment volume growth positive in Q3 with high-single-digit organic growth in H2 - a period that sits inside MillerKnoll's fiscal Q1 (1 June - 29 August 2026), against a Q1 FY26 comparison of consolidated orders -5.4% and North America Contract orders -8.2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders alone have NOT paid on this name and I have sized for that: on 2026-03-25 North America Contract orders printed +13.1% reported and the stock fell 22.37% on a $0.02 EPS miss; on 2026-06-24 orders printed -6.3% with backlog -10.8% and the stock rose 12.01% on an EPS beat at the top of guidance. So the order line is only worth anything here through the FY27 guide ($3.93-4.13bn, ~5% growth), which is why I file this under guidance rather than reported_quarter: what an accelerating industry order rate buys is that the guide survives contact with an entering backlog down 10.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: MillerKnoll is covered by three analysts (two Buy at a $35 mean target, StoneX at Hold) and the consensus EPS has been flat for 60 days, so nothing in the estimate record shows the HNI read-through being taken. If it had been, the stock would not have de-rated 10.9% over the month while the business-services peer group fell 1.7%, and the pre-print article on the wire this morning would not be framing the quarter as a cost-inflation margin test with no mention of order momentum. HNI is also a different shareholder base - a $4bn+ industrial - and MillerKnoll's own last-reported order line (-10.0% North America) is the number the tape is anchored on.
findings.independence: Second, unrelated source: StoneX's August 2026 Commercial Dealer Survey, reported as showing 'continued resilience of demand and optimism for future demand' (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/millerknoll-earnings-in-focus-as-new-ceo-faces-margin-test-93CH-4909208, 2026-09-21) - the dealer channel both companies sell through, and notably it comes from the one analyst on this name who is NOT a Buy. Net of the rest of the company: this evidence covers North America Contract plus International Contract, roughly 70% of revenue. The other ~30% is Global Retail, where the direct read-through is RH calling this 'the worst housing market in four decades' while still printing +2.6% revenue and guiding FY26 to +5.5-7.0% - low growth, not a collapse, consistent with MillerKnoll's own Global Retail orders +2.0% organic last quarter. I have trimmed the size for that 30% rather than sizing on the contract read alone. Cuts the other way at a longer horizon: the AIA/Deltek ABI was 47.2 in August with an 18th consecutive monthly decline in design contracts (https://archinect.com/news/article/150500752/architecture-billings-index-reports-continued-soft-business-conditions-in-august) - that leads contract furniture by 9-12 months, so it bears on FY28 and is in every furniture preview already; I dropped it as a separate finding rather than double-count the same demand line in two directions.

findings.finding: The FY26 10-K discloses that the Global Retail reporting unit's fair value exceeded carrying value by just 1.1%, International Contract by 3.1%, and the Muuto and Knoll indefinite-lived trade names by 2.1% and 6.8% - cushions thin enough that the company says 'relatively modest adverse changes' in projected revenue growth or margin would produce material impairment charges, and MillerKnoll has form for taking interim impairments mid-year when performance disappoints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The direct precedent is MillerKnoll's own: in Q3 FY25 management identified interim triggering events and took $30.1m (Global Retail) and $62.2m (Holly Hunt) of non-cash goodwill impairment - and the stock rose 10.69% on that print (baseline, 2026-03-26... corrected: 2025-03-26, +10.69%). The market looked straight through a $92m charge. That history is the whole reason this is sized at -0.4 and not at -2: the charge itself is not what this stock pays for, and it only matters as a signal that management has cut the Global Retail plan, which would show up in the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: A 1.1% cushion is a critical-audit-matter footnote in a 250-page 10-K filed in July on a three-analyst name; no aggregator carries reporting-unit cushion percentages and no preview mentions it. If it were priced, the forward PE would not be 10.0 with two of three analysts at a $35 target - a 69% upside target is not what a book carrying a near-zero goodwill cushion on 30% of revenue looks like.
findings.independence: None that is genuinely independent. This rests on the SAME document as the IEEPA finding above (the FY26 10-K) and I say so here rather than let the sum treat them as two corroborating reads - they are two different disclosures in one filing, and only the refund one has an outside corroborator. The honest weakness, which is why the number is small: the impairment is a hypothesis about what management will decide this quarter, not a fact about the print, and the one time it happened the stock went up.

outside_window.finding: The Section 232 tariff on imported wood and upholstered wooden furniture stays at 25% but the scheduled step-up to 30%, deferred on 5 January 2026, now takes effect 1 January 2027 - inside FY27 and a live question for the FY27 gross-margin bridge, but nothing about it resolves on 22 September.

A permanent CEO appointment - the board began a search with an external firm when Andi Owen retired on 30 June 2026 and Jeff Stutz became interim CEO; a named successor is a rebasing risk to the inherited FY27 guide, but there is no evidence it lands with this print.

searched_and_found_nothing: Input-cost inflation, which is the frame the only pre-print article uses ('34% increases in raw material expenses', steel and fuel): US hot-rolled coil was ~$1,220/MT in June 2026 and ~$1,213/MT in September 2026, i.e. flat since the guide was set (https://www.procurementresource.com/resource-center/hot-rolled-steel-price-trends). The bear narrative on the wire is not supported by the underlying commodity for this quarter, so I filed no cost finding in either direction - a commodity-to-margin inference is a hypothesis, not a finding.
BIFMA monthly shipment and order statistics for July/August 2026 - members-only, no public release found for the months inside MillerKnoll's fiscal Q1.
Steelcase as a read-through: it no longer reports, having been acquired by HNI (merger agreement 2025-08-03), so the usual same-week competitor print does not exist this quarter.

Any 13D/activist filing, any debt refinancing or covenant amendment 8-K, any dividend change - the only 8-K since the June results is an Item 5.03 bylaw amendment (2026-07-20) and the dividend is unchanged at $0.1875.

Herman Miller / Design Within Reach store-opening announcements against the FY27 plan of 9-11 and 5-7 openings - the company newsroom carries no store opening between 24 June and 21 September 2026 (only a DWR pop-up on 8 June), which is suggestive of a back-loaded cadence but is absence of a press release, not evidence, so it is not filed.
A company-level quantification of IEEPA duties actually paid - not disclosed anywhere in the 10-K, the releases or the transcripts; only net-of-mitigation gross-margin impacts are given.
baseline_tension: My read cuts against the baseline's +9.66 skew and agrees with the free control: the 20-day run-up of -12.38% ranks this name long on -run_up, and I am long. The skew is the number I have to answer for, and the answer is that there is no option market here - 75 contracts of total open interest and an ATM spread 80% of mid, which the baseline itself flags - so the 'downside paid' lean and the 16.78% implied move are artefacts of two wide quotes rather than anything anyone paid for, and I anchor on the 10.83% median realised reaction instead.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (size one-offs as one-offs) cut the IEEPA refund from +2.2 to +1.2: the file's own record is four names carrying a tariff-refund thesis where the refund landed in all four and the reaction split entirely on guidance direction. I have no stated path from this refund to the FY27 guide, so it stays filed as one_off at a fraction of the dollars.

Lesson 1 (the reaction function has veto power) re-filed the demand finding from reported_quarter to guidance and cut it from +1.5 to +1.3: this name's last two prints show the order line being ignored or inverted (+13.1% orders and -22.4%; -6.3% orders and +12.0%), so accelerating industry orders are only worth something here through whether the FY27 guide survives.

Lesson 2's impairment clause moved the goodwill-cushion finding from one_off to reported_quarter, and checking the reaction history it demands cut it from -0.7 to -0.4: MillerKnoll's own $92.3m of interim impairments in Q3 FY25 bought a +10.69% print.

Dropped the AIA/Deltek ABI finding (-0.5 in the draft) entirely on two grounds: it is in every furniture preview so it is wire copy, and it addresses a 9-12 month horizon while my positive demand finding addresses the current quarter - keeping both would have been the self-contradicting set lesson 3 and lesson 5 warn about. It survives as a horizon caveat inside the demand finding's independence field instead.

Lesson 8 (thin coverage means a confirmed fact moves more) plus lesson 3's requirement that the caveat reach the number moved expected_move from +3.0 to +3.5 and made me state explicitly WHY it sits above the findings sum of +2.1 rather than leaving the gap unexplained: three analysts, a 10.83% median reaction, 7.29 days to cover, and a bar the company itself guided down 20% y/y.
Lesson 9 (net of the rest) added the explicit 70% contract / 30% Global Retail split and the RH housing read-through into the demand finding's sizing, rather than sizing the contract read gross.

Lesson 7 was read and left the sizes standing: short interest at 5.99% of float is not crowded enough to shrink anything, and the skew is disowned on the option book's own thinness rather than discounted.
